text:
Calgary and Los Angeles both arrive on slides. The Flames lost 3-1 to the Rangers on Wednesday and are 2-2-1 in their last five, without Kevin Bahl and Connor Zary. The Kings have dropped three straight and are 1-4-0 over five, most recently 5-2 to the Islanders. Kevin Fiala made his season debut in that game, and Erik Gustafsson is day-to-day and could return.

The Kings' record flatters no one, but our numbers like them more than the standings do. They've taken 57% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in those five games, and 51% at five on five this season, against 47% for Calgary. Finishing and goaltending have cost them. Los Angeles has the better power play (0.80 expected goals a game to 0.39), though the Kings take 4.2 penalties a game. In net, projected starters Dustin Wolf (-6.6 goals saved above expected this season) and Darcy Kuemper (-7.6) are both below par. Kuemper was also 6.8 below last year, Wolf 2.8.

Watch Artemi Panarin, 74% for a point, and Quinton Byfield, 32% to score and two points from 200 career. For Calgary, Matt Coronato is one goal from 50, and Joel Farabee is 58% for a point. Our under-the-radar picks: Farabee, with his ice time up, and Corey Perry, 19% to score on the fourth line, where his shots have been dangerous.
